themes.name: Growth Mindset and Heightened Awareness
themes.description: The coaching process repeatedly emphasizes that professional growth involves feeling less certain as awareness increases, which is a natural part of adopting new dialogic practices. This mindset supports teachers in embracing the challenges of shifting to student-centered talk.
supportingQuotes: Sometimes, the more we learn, the more we feel that we know less. That’s because we are more aware of what we are doing.

themes.name: Language as a Barrier to STEM and Dialogic Participation
themes.description: Teachers identify that students' limited English vocabulary and comprehension impede their ability to engage in STEM reasoning and dialogic talk, raising questions about the role of language proficiency in STEM mastery.
supportingQuotes: Adakah penguasaan bahasa inggeris akan mempengaruhi penguasaan kemahiran STEM murid-murid ? atau adakah bahasa itu yang membuat murid itu berjaya dalam menguasai STEM?
Pupils forgot or confused (?) about the terms more than, less than, larger and smaller. 'reserve' not commonly used in previous class, drift terms / words.

themes.name: Scaffolding Student Talk through Pre-teaching and Sentence Frames
themes.description: Coaches support teachers in using pre-teaching of key vocabulary and sentence frames to enable students to participate in dialogic exchanges, thereby managing student talk in English more effectively.
supportingQuotes: I shared sentence frames that help students respond in class. I shared the idea of pre-teaching the vocabulary around less or more, units, tens and to ask students to reply to those before moving on so that understanding of the key vocabulary is secured

themes.name: Active Engagement Strategies to Foster Dialogic Interaction
themes.description: Teachers implement interactive activities like gallery walks and sticky notes to encourage student questioning and higher-order thinking, shifting away from lecture-based instruction and promoting student talk.
supportingQuotes: The use of sticky notes encouraged pupils to think critically, ask meaningful questions, and develop higher-order thinking skills (HOTS).

themes.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Instructional Change
themes.description: Teachers engage in deep reflection on lesson outcomes and commit to concrete changes, such as providing handouts and guided practice, to better support student talk and understanding in STEM.
supportingQuotes: I found out what I missed out in this lesson. Handouts were not given, not guidance from me for them to experience or do the actual vertical form in real time. Class was basically questions and answers session instead of actual 'do-it' session.

themes.name: Language barriers and translation dependency
themes.description: Teachers and students struggle with English proficiency in DLP classrooms, leading to reliance on native language translation and limited English use outside formal settings.
supportingQuotes: They are still learning on how to respond using English, but there's have been a little bit of improvement compared to before
Jika tak faham perlu menterjemahkan (If not understood, translation is necessary)
Anthony is not confident in English and so are his students.

themes.name: Scaffolding dialogic strategies through structured talk and peer support
themes.description: Coaching promotes structured talk techniques such as think-pair-share, mixed-ability grouping, and revoicing to increase student talk and conceptual understanding.
supportingQuotes: Choosing students with low confidence to answer. Supporting less confident students with the stronger students in groups
This happened when I asked the stronger students to Think-Pair-Share with the weaker students. The weakest students were able to explain and this was surprising.
We discussed using mixed ability pairs and we may continue to look at scaffolding in the next session.

themes.name: Pedagogical barriers from misconceptions and insufficient wait time
themes.description: Students exhibit persistent STEM misconceptions (e.g., fraction representation) and inadequate wait time hinders deeper processing, requiring adjusted pacing and concrete examples.
supportingQuotes: Still have the mindset of coloured region as numerator and non-coloured region as denominator, so instead of 2/3, it became 2/1, wrong concept.
This date highlighted that a 30-second wait time was insufficient for conceptual processing.
will try giving more wait time, and look at time management - according to time card as wait time 30s is too short. 1 minute should be appropriate.

themes.name: Coaching as a catalyst for goal-setting and reflective practice
themes.description: Instructional coaching uses specific feedback, student-centred goal setting, and tools like confidence surveys to guide teachers' reflective practice and improve dialogic teaching.
supportingQuotes: I named the strategy and I recapped and summarised what I heard. I asked Habib to recognise the moment of change, and then asked if I could share that with him.
The confidence survey helped pinpoint areas for growth and helped us see opportunities to create more inclusive classrooms...

Mostly teachers have a hard time thinking of goals, but they all agree that students need to speak more, also that we need to better evaluate their progress in speaking (independantly, away from chorusing).

themes.name: Creative strategies to amplify student voice and engagement
themes.description: Teachers use innovative methods like the 'walkie-talkie' to encourage shy students to speak, visibly increasing engagement and focus on the speaker, which supports the adoption of dialogic strategies in managing student talk.
supportingQuotes: The student confidently used the walkie-talkie in class... I noted how other children were genuinely excited about this and were all focused on the student talking.
Walkie-Talkie absolutely forces this, listen to how quiet they are when it is used.

themes.name: Shifting from teacher-led to student-centered talk
themes.description: Teachers are moving away from immediate answers and teacher-led instruction toward giving students time to think, discuss, and explain reasoning, which increases student confidence in using English mathematical terms.
supportingQuotes: I changed my habit from immediately giving students answers to giving them time to think and discuss with their friends first. After that, the students became more active, more of them tried to answer, and their confidence level increased when using Mathematical terms in English.

themes.name: Barriers: English proficiency and teacher beliefs
themes.description: Teachers perceive students' English proficiency as a limitation to attainment and struggle to scaffold talk, while some teachers remain attached to teacher-led methods for control, hindering the adoption of dialogic strategies.
supportingQuotes: Habit: teacher believes student attainment is limited by the students' English proficiency
he thinks that his use of the whiteboard to engage students is effective becuase it enables him to have control.

themes.name: Coaching through observation and specific feedback
themes.description: Coaches use video analysis and targeted feedback to identify progress and set goals, enabling focused and effective coaching conversations that support teachers in implementing dialogic strategies.
supportingQuotes: Video observation allows real focused and targeted responses.
I described, summarized what occurred and then identified where the goals previously discussed were met.

themes.name: Contextual interruptions and competing priorities
themes.description: School events like exams and revision disrupt the continuity of dialogic practice, and lesson planning can overshadow the focus on dialogic strategies, presenting pedagogical barriers to sustained implementation.
supportingQuotes: Did not try anything, said that there were exams going on.
The lesson plan was a good task but it took away the emphasis from dialogic strategies as we started working on pedagogy.

themes.name: Structured dialogic routines to manage student talk
themes.description: Coaching encouraged teachers to implement structured routines like Think-Pair-Share and sentence frames to scaffold student dialogue and manage participation, including redistributing talk among students.
supportingQuotes: Target set to keep Think-Pair-Share (T-P-S) going with time limits. (Healery, coaching conversation)
Habib used laminated sentence frames to give confidence to students speaking English. redistributing dominating students balanced group participation. (Habib, 2026-07-09)

themes.name: Language scaffolding for English medium instruction (DLP)
themes.description: Teachers used explicit language scaffolds such as a star system for transitioning from native languages to English, and students expressed a preference for immersive English exposure to build academic vocabulary.
supportingQuotes: Students can answer in Iban/Malay but teacher to introduce star system over time - ★1 star for Iban explanation; ★★2 stars for mix Iban/English explanation; ★★★3 stars for English explanation (Healery, Jul 06, 2026)
Cikgu selalu bercakap Inggeris (Student survey, Jul 07, 2026)

themes.name: Gradual release of responsibility and reduced direct instruction
themes.description: Coaching supported teachers in shifting from teacher-led instruction to models like 'I Do, We Do, You Do' and chunking lessons, which helped students take more ownership of learning.
keywords: I Do We Do You Do
supportingQuotes: The lesson implements the gradual release of responsibility model ("I Do, We Do, You Do"). (Healery, Jul 06, 2026)
Lesson chunking and reducing direct instruction worked well. (Habib, 2026-07-02)

themes.name: Pedagogical barriers from abstract language and time constraints
themes.description: Teachers encountered barriers when using abstract metaphors and when vocabulary activities consumed too much time, hindering student understanding and lesson pacing.
supportingQuotes: LO was not achieved, vertical forms (number of floors), not all pupils can recognised it. ... Pupils forgot or confused (?) about the terms more than, less than, larger and smaller. (Habib, undated division artifact)
tried a vocabulary starter that enthused students but took longer than expected. (Healery, 2026-07-09)

themes.name: Adoption of Dialogic Questioning Strategies
themes.description: Teachers are explicitly deploying open-ended, student-centered questions to stimulate discussion and reasoning in the STEM lesson, indicating uptake of dialogic teaching techniques.
supportingQuotes: Why do you think so?
Could someone build on what was just said?
Did anyone get a different answer?

themes.name: Reflective Practice as a Coaching-Enabled Process
themes.description: Coaching appears to foster deep self-questioning about instructional decisions and student responses, as seen in post-lesson reflections that probe missed opportunities and satisfaction with practice.
supportingQuotes: Why did I do that? Why didn’t I say this?
Am I satisfied with how we used our time in the class?
Do I really respond in the best way to student questions?

themes.name: Pedagogical Barrier: Managing Diverse Learning Paces and Inclusivity
themes.description: Teachers face significant challenges in balancing the needs of students with varied learning paces and physical abilities against rigid curriculum goals, a barrier that coaching must address to support equitable dialogic participation.
supportingQuotes: One of the main hurdles is managing groups with diverse learning pace and physical abilities. It can be difficul to ensure every individuals feel included while still meeting overall cuniculum goals.

themes.name: Structured Time Management for Student Talk
themes.description: Dialogic lessons are deliberately structured with timed segments for teacher prompt, student discussion, and synthesis, while reflections question the effectiveness of time use, highlighting time as a key factor in managing student talk.
supportingQuotes: Am I satisfied with how we used our time in the class?
structured into a 1-minute teacher prompt, a 3-minute student-led dialogic discussion, and a 1-minute synthesis closure

themes.name: Bilingual Scaffolding for Dialogic Talk
themes.description: Teachers use both English and Malay prompts to support student participation in the English-medium DLP context, indicating a translanguaging approach to scaffold dialogic interaction.
supportingQuotes: Bolehkah seseorang membina apa yang baru sahaja katakan? / Could someone build on what was just said?
Adakah sesiapa mendapat jawapan yang berbeza? / Did anyone get a different answer?

# Complete Triangulated Sarawak Instructional Coaching Corpus Chronological records across 6 teachers and 3 coaches (83 records). --- ### [2025-04-01] Artifact Review: Anthony (Apr 01, 2025) Apr 01, 2025: Baseline evaluation sets benchmarks across 5 core domains. --- ### [2026-03-17] Artifact Review: Carolyne (Mar 17, 2026) Mar 17, 2026 – Lesson Plan: Strategies 1 (Human Organs) Artifact Type: Formative Lesson Plan & Reflection Substance: Implemented a movement-based "Gallery Walk" activity targeting Year 4A human organ functions. Students collaborated in groups of 6–7 to sketch organ diagrams on Mahjong paper and utilized sticky notes to generate peer-to-peer questions. The lesson reflection notes that 85% of pupils successfully achieved the learning standard, though a small sub-segment required targeted scaffolding to explain complex physiological functions confidently. Coaching Implication: Illustrates successful execution of active engagement strategies, shifting the classroom dynamic away from a traditional lecture model. Key Quotation: "The use of sticky notes encouraged pupils to think critically, ask meaningful questions, and develop higher-order thinking skills (HOTS)." --- ### [2026-04-01] Artifact Review: Anis (Apr 2026) 1. Apr 2026 — Anis Baseline (Diagnostic Self-Assessment) Coaching Context & Analysis: This artifact serves as the foundational diagnostic layer for the coaching engagement. It establishes a 1–4 metric scoring system spanning five core pedagogical domains: Dialogic Teaching, Use of English for Instruction, Assessment for Learning, Reflective Practice, and Leading Professional Development. The coaching focus centers heavily on a growth mindset and the cognitive dissonance that often accompanies professional upskilling. It explicitly isolates target competencies around student-led explanation, reasoning language, intentional talk activities, pre-teaching vocabulary, and structured outputs. Verbatim Key Quotation:> "Sometimes, the more we learn, the more we feel that we know less. That’s because we are more aware of what we are doing." --- ### [2026-04-01] Artifact Review: Carolyne (Apr 2026) Apr 2026 – Baseline Scores Document Artifact Type: Teacher Self-Assessment Profile Substance: This profile documents Carolyne’s initial self-assessment against 5 instructional domains on a scale of 1 to 4 (Emerging to Excelling). The core focus areas include Dialogic Teaching, Assessment for Learning (AFL), and Use of English for Instruction. The tool explicitly reminds the teacher that perceived shifts backward or plateaus are a natural consequence of heightened pedagogical awareness. Coaching Implication: Provides the structural criteria used by the instructional coach to anchor subsequent feedback cycles and lesson plan reviews. supportingQuotes: Why do you think so?
Could someone build on what was just said?
Did anyone get a different answer?

themes.name: Reflective Practice and Self-Evaluation
themes.description: Post-lesson coaching reflections reveal teachers critically questioning their instructional choices and responsiveness to students, indicating coaching's role in fostering deep self-evaluation.
supportingQuotes: Why did I do that? Why didn’t I say this?
Am I satisfied with how we used our time in the class?
Do I really respond in the best way to student questions?

themes.name: Pedagogical Barriers in Diverse Learner Management
themes.description: Teachers report challenges balancing individual inclusivity with rigid curriculum goals when managing groups with diverse learning paces, which can hinder effective dialogic engagement.
supportingQuotes: One of the main hurdles is managing groups with diverse learning pace and physical abilities. It can be difficul to ensure every individuals feel included while still meeting overall cuniculum goals.

themes.name: Structured Time Allocation for Dialogic Talk
themes.description: The lesson plan explicitly segments time for teacher prompts, student-led discussion, and synthesis, demonstrating deliberate design to manage and maximize student talk within the STEM lesson.
supportingQuotes: structured into a 1-minute teacher prompt, a 3-minute student-led dialogic discussion, and a 1-minute synthesis closure

Students collaborated in groups of 6–7 to sketch organ diagrams on Mahjong paper and utilized sticky notes to generate peer-to-peer questions. The lesson reflection notes that 85% of pupils successfully achieved the learning standard, though a small sub-segment required targeted scaffolding to explain complex physiological functions confidently. Coaching Implication: Illustrates successful execution of active engagement strategies, shifting the classroom dynamic away from a traditional lecture model. The coaching focus centers heavily on a growth mindset and the cognitive dissonance that often accompanies professional upskilling. It explicitly isolates target competencies around student-led explanation, reasoning language, intentional talk activities, pre-teaching vocabulary, and structured outputs.
